*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: {{workspace:person/maya-desai-v2}}/knowledge/people/maya-desai/onboarding-plan.md
+# Maya Desai — Senior Platform Engineer onboarding plan
+
+Status: reviewed draft; personal branch only; access approvals remain pending.
+
+## Role and boundaries
+
+Maya joins Ethan Park's Platform & Console team as a Senior Platform Engineer, focused on the LiteLLM gateway and Langfuse operations console. Her initial remit is gateway policy, request validation/routing, telemetry propagation, and operator-console workflows. She may develop and review changes in local, test, and approved staging environments. She must not receive production, customer-data, secret-write, protected-branch, release, or upstream-maintainer privileges by implication of title.
+
+The team owns inference gateway policy, tenant configuration, safe rollouts, telemetry workflows, and operator-facing console behavior. Runtime kernels/model code, billing policy, security policy, and telemetry-platform infrastructure remain with their respective owners; changes crossing those boundaries require their review. [Platform & Console brief, `curated_024986ded9ae947c8913f2eb`](/knowledge/curated/team-platform-console/brief.md)
+
+## First week: access and local setup
+
+1. Ethan files the canonical `ONBOARD-ACCESS` request using the least-privilege role template, naming only LiteLLM, Langfuse, the team Jira board, internal docs, and read-only operational dashboards. People Ops owns provisioning; Ethan owns role correctness. Target: Okta/Slack within 2 hours of acknowledgement, GitHub/GCP invites within 4 hours, and verified core tooling within 8 business hours. Escalate after 8 business hours. Production or protected-resource access requires a separate privilege-escalation ticket and Security approval; Security's review target is two business days and production requests should allow 48–72 hours. [Contributor Toolflow and Privileges Playbook, `dsid_7754cd5d7b4d4a7ea217f1c09c28ef3`](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/contributor-toolflow-and-privileges-playbook-2026.json)
+2. Verify SSO and 2FA, GitHub identity, repo clone, Jira board, Confluence, and read-only dashboard access. Do not place credentials in shell history, repository files, examples, screenshots, or tickets.
+3. Use fork-based branches until specific org branch permissions are approved. Confirm `gh auth status` and `git remote -v`; set `origin` to Maya's fork and keep `upstream` read-only. Fork workflows may require a maintainer to authorize CI; never attempt to bypass branch protection or enable secret-bearing jobs before review. [New-hire branch-policy thread, `dsid_4ae8b9d4ba5a4003b3d1ca812544c86e`](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/new-hires/1987654321-initial-access-403-push-branch-policy.json)
+4. LiteLLM: fork and clone, create a conventional feature branch, run `make install-dev`, optionally `make install-hooks`, and verify `make help`. Backend work requires at least one test, `make lint`, and `make test-unit`; proxy/E2E work may require `make install-test-deps`. Start locally with `make install-proxy-dev` and `uv run litellm --config <local-config>`. Never use live provider keys in unit tests. [LiteLLM contributor guide, `enterprise_b9e03890a22cfc276b5468d4`](/code/litellm/CONTRIBUTING.md); [LiteLLM E2E guide, `enterprise_ffc0390514a198a0f0bb9f75`](/code/litellm/tests/e2e/CONTRIBUTING.md)
+5. Langfuse: follow the repository's documented container/service topology and contribution setup; use synthetic local data only. Validate the affected web, worker, shared-package, or ingestion path with the repository-prescribed lint, type, unit, build, and migration checks. [Langfuse contributor guide, `enterprise_30981ba0dc3b4760e378333b`](/code/langfuse/CONTRIBUTING.md)
+
+## Repository ownership and review
+
+- LiteLLM gateway/proxy: Maya implements scoped changes; Benji Okafor is primary gateway/control-plane mentor and first reviewer. Kaitlyn Nguyen reviews authentication, authorization, API-key, tenancy, and security-sensitive changes. Ethan is manager approver and resolves scope or ownership disputes.
+- Langfuse operations console: Maya owns assigned integration work; Chloe Martin is console-backend approver, while Jada Williams is the console/UI reviewer for user-facing flows. Logan Wright or the telemetry-platform owner reviews trace schemas, ingestion, dashboard, and cardinality changes.
+- Cross-cutting contracts: Allison Grant reviews API standards; Security must approve new privilege, secret, customer-data, or production paths. The current review pattern explicitly routes console, telemetry, versioning/auth, API-contract, and SRE concerns to the corresponding roles. [Cost-model schema review, `dsid_bda5fd8434594774ad119e061549a717`](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1768721444.json)
+
+## Safe upstream issue handling
+
+Treat upstream repositories as external collaboration surfaces. Reproduce with synthetic data, search for duplicates, and record impact without Redwood customer names, tenant IDs, logs, traces, internal URLs, credentials, unreleased roadmap, or security-sensitive configuration. Before opening or commenting on an upstream issue, link an internal triage ticket and obtain a Redwood maintainer/owner review. Security vulnerabilities follow the upstream private security channel, never a public issue.
+
+Keep PRs isolated to one problem, sign the required CLA, add tests, and target the base branch named by the current upstream guide. Do not add fork-only dependencies or run secret-bearing workflows from an unreviewed fork; coordinate with a maintainer when canonical-repository action is required. [LiteLLM contributor guide, `enterprise_b9e03890a22cfc276b5468d4`](/code/litellm/CONTRIBUTING.md); [LiteLLM fork dependency guard, `enterprise_1b22429b54258d6ee86f6bc0`](/code/litellm/.github/workflows/guard-fork-dependencies.yml); [New-hire branch-policy thread, `dsid_4ae8b9d4ba5a4003b3d1ca812544c86e`](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/new-hires/1987654321-initial-access-403-push-branch-policy.json)
+
+## First 30 days
+
+- Days 1–3: complete access verification, security onboarding, both local builds, and one synthetic request/trace from LiteLLM through the local Langfuse stack. Document failures; do not request production as a workaround.
+- Days 4–7: pair with Benji on a gateway code walk and Chloe/Jada on a console code walk. Trace request metadata, auth, telemetry ingestion, worker processing, and operator UI. Select a low-risk docs/test or support-reproduction change.
+- Week 2: deliver the small change through fork PR, with tests and owner approvals. Reproduce the open dashboard label-compatibility support follow-up and confirm the universal dashboard patch and CI rename guard have owners; do not touch customer data. [Console throughput support escalation, `dsid_3518922f85074831b0d0201264294dd1`](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/support/2050001234-urgent-escalation-console-thruput-rows-zeroed-after-label-shift.json)
+- Week 3: own a scoped LiteLLM-to-Langfuse telemetry improvement or operator-console bug. Validate compatibility, bounded cardinality, failure behavior, and rollback. Present the design to gateway, console, and telemetry owners.
+- Week 4: ship or reach merge-ready status, update the runbook/codebase map, and lead a synthetic game-day or replay. Align the next milestone to telemetry convergence: canonical signals, operator-first dashboards, synthetic validation, and migration with reconciliation rather than parallel ingestion. [Operator Telemetry Convergence roadmap, `dsid_4a5f521dd19f40b3b9d680a1b7776280`](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-platform/roadmap/operator-telemetry-convergence-skill-roadmap-2026.json)
+
+## Mentors, approvers, and validation
+
+- Manager and final scope approver: Ethan Park.
+- Gateway mentor/reviewer: Benji Okafor; auth/security reviewer: Kaitlyn Nguyen.
+- Console mentor/approver: Chloe Martin; UI reviewer: Jada Williams.
+- Telemetry reviewer: Logan Wright / telemetry-platform.
+- Org escalation: Priya Natarajan. Privilege approval: Security. Provisioning owner: People Ops.
+
+Completion evidence is: core access verified; production/elevated access explicitly absent or ticket-approved; both local stacks start; synthetic gateway-to-trace flow succeeds; required lint/unit/build checks pass; first PR has code-owner review; no sensitive data appears in upstream artifacts; support reproduction and rollback notes are attached; and Ethan records the 30-day review.
+
+## Approval gaps at creation
+
+No evidence in the reviewed sources confirms Maya's actual Okta/GitHub/GCP/Datadog/Jira grants, LiteLLM or Langfuse team membership, protected-branch rights, staging access, CI-secret authorization, production/customer-data access, on-call placement, or Security approval. All remain pending and must be validated through the access ticket. The personal knowledge branch must remain isolated until those approvals are complete.
*** Add File: {{workspace:person/maya-desai-v2}}/knowledge/teams/platform-console/codebase-map.md
+# Platform & Console codebase map: LiteLLM and Langfuse
+
+Status: reviewed ownership map for onboarding and code triage. Role mappings describe review responsibility, not automatic access.
+
+| Repository / subsystem | Redwood responsible role(s) | Review and validation evidence |
+|---|---|---|
+| LiteLLM proxy/gateway, routing, request validation, quotas | Ethan Park (manager/scope); Benji Okafor (control-plane mentor); Amara Diallo (API gateway); Cole Summers (quota/metering) | Team remit includes gateway policy and tenant configuration [`curated_024986ded9ae947c8913f2eb`](/knowledge/curated/team-platform-console/brief.md). Directory roles identify control-plane, gateway, and quota ownership [`knowledge/company/employee_directory.yaml`](/knowledge/company/employee_directory.yaml). |
+| LiteLLM authn/authz, API keys, tenant isolation | Kaitlyn Nguyen; Security for privilege or secret boundary changes | Role directory and schema-review routing identify Kaitlyn for versioning/auth implications [`dsid_bda5fd8434594774ad119e061549a717`](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1768721444.json). |
+| LiteLLM tests and upstream contribution workflow | Change author plus Benji/code owner; maintainer for canonical CI or dependency changes | Backend changes require tests, lint, unit checks, focused scope, and CLA [`enterprise_b9e03890a22cfc276b5468d4`](/code/litellm/CONTRIBUTING.md); E2E setup is separately documented [`enterprise_ffc0390514a198a0f0bb9f75`](/code/litellm/tests/e2e/CONTRIBUTING.md); fork dependency changes are blocked pending maintainer coordination [`enterprise_1b22429b54258d6ee86f6bc0`](/code/litellm/.github/workflows/guard-fork-dependencies.yml). |
+| LiteLLM ↔ Langfuse tracing/OTel integration | Maya as assigned implementer; Logan Wright / telemetry-platform as telemetry owner; gateway owner for emission semantics | Team remit covers telemetry workflows; roadmap requires one telemetry source of truth, canonical signals, reconciliation, bounded/noise-aware operator views [`dsid_4a5f521dd19f40b3b9d680a1b7776280`](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-platform/roadmap/operator-telemetry-convergence-skill-roadmap-2026.json). |
+| Langfuse web/operator console | Chloe Martin (console-backend approver); Jada Williams (console/UI reviewer); Maya for assigned integration work | Console is the operator-facing surface [`curated_024986ded9ae947c8913f2eb`](/knowledge/curated/team-platform-console/brief.md); cross-team review explicitly requests Chloe/Jada for Console [`dsid_bda5fd8434594774ad119e061549a717`](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1768721444.json). |
+| Langfuse worker/ingestion, shared trace schema, dashboards | Logan Wright / telemetry-platform; Chloe for console contract; SRE for alert/runbook impact | The roadmap assigns telemetry ownership and requires synthetic validation/game days [`dsid_4a5f521dd19f40b3b9d680a1b7776280`](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-platform/roadmap/operator-telemetry-convergence-skill-roadmap-2026.json). |
+| Langfuse local architecture, migrations, builds and tests | Change author; subsystem code owner; Chloe or Logan according to path | Canonical architecture and contributor setup are in the repository guide [`enterprise_30981ba0dc3b4760e378333b`](/code/langfuse/CONTRIBUTING.md). |
+| Cross-repo API/schema compatibility | Allison Grant (API standards); Kaitlyn Nguyen (compat/auth); Chloe/Jada (console); Logan/Nadia (telemetry); SRE for deterministic failure signals | The cost-model contract review establishes additive compatibility, explicit versions/units, tolerant clients, bounded cardinality, and routed approval roles [`dsid_bda5fd8434594774ad119e061549a717`](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-platform/1768721444.json). |
+| Production access, secrets, customer data, protected branches | Security approves privilege; Ethan supplies justification; People Ops implements standard grants; repository maintainers control protected workflows | Least privilege, auditable tickets, 8-business-hour core target, two-business-day escalation review, and 48–72-hour production lead time are canonical policy [`dsid_7754cd5d7b4d4a7ea217f1c09c28ef3c`](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/contributor-toolflow-and-privileges-playbook-2026.json). |
+| Active support: console throughput rows after metric-label shift | Platform/telemetry owner for compatibility and CI guard; console owner for dashboard migration | P0 compatibility hotfix is recorded done; open P1 work is universal dashboard migration and a CI check for label renames [`dsid_3518922f85074831b0d0201264294dd1`](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/support/2050001234-urgent-escalation-console-thruput-rows-zeroed-after-label-shift.json). |
+
+## Triage route
+
+1. Classify the issue by path and impact: gateway, auth/tenant, trace ingestion, worker, console, schema, or support.
+2. Reproduce locally with synthetic data and record exact versions. Never paste customer or secret material into public upstream systems.
+3. Assign the path owner above and add cross-cutting reviewers for auth, telemetry, API compatibility, SRE, or Security.
+4. For upstream work, create/link the internal ticket first, deduplicate, obtain owner review, and use the fork/PR workflow. Escalate vulnerabilities privately.
+5. Validate with repository checks plus contract compatibility, bounded cardinality, failure/rollback behavior, and a synthetic end-to-end trace where relevant.
+6. Production, protected workflow, secret, or customer-data actions remain blocked until the corresponding auditable approval exists.
+
+## Current priority lens
+
+Prefer work that converges canonical telemetry, reduces duplicate/noisy signals, improves operator-first dashboards/runbooks, preserves schema compatibility, and validates changes through synthetic scenarios and reconciliation. Do not expand into runtime kernel changes or billing redesign; those are explicitly outside the telemetry program's scope. [`dsid_4a5f521dd19f40b3b9d680a1b7776280`](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-platform/roadmap/operator-telemetry-convergence-skill-roadmap-2026.json)
*** End Patch
